commands.name: skill:jev
commands.description: Ask Jev — TypeSafe's System One model, served on the OpenCode Zen key — typed questions and get calibrated probabilities back. Use for classification, routing, ranking, extraction checks, verification, or any yes/no/pick/score judgment your code branches on. Trigger on "jev", "typesafe", "system one", "noul", "calibrated probability", "ask jev", or a request to score/classify/route something with a confidence value.

commands.name: skill:logisim-evolution
commands.description: Design, inspect, edit, simulate, test, and debug Logisim Evolution digital circuits directly through native .circ XML, test-vector files, the CLI, and the desktop GUI. Use for logic gates, buses, subcircuits, adders, multiplexers, registers, counters, ROM/RAM, truth tables, circuit repair, and Logisim automation without MCP.

commands.name: skill:unslop
commands.description: Remove AI writing patterns from prose using either audit-only detection or a two-pass rewrite flow (diagnosis then reconstruction). Use this skill when editing, reviewing, or rewriting AI-generated content to make it sound human. Triggers on requests to "humanize", "de-slop", "fix AI text", "make it sound human", "remove AI patterns", or when reviewing text that contains obvious AI tells like "Here's the thing:", "Let that sink in", or "In today's fast-paced landscape". Also use when the user pastes text and says it "sounds like ChatGPT", "sounds robotic", "needs to sound more natural", or asks you to "clean up" drafted content before publishing.

commands.name: skill:unslop-ui
commands.description: Strips the cues that make a website read as AI-generated and forces a deliberate, project-specific design choice instead of the model's default. It does not impose a look or hand you taste. It removes tells (default shadcn/Tailwind, AI-purple gradients, gradient heading text, unprompted neon glow, emoji-as-icons, the centered hero plus three feature cards) AND the newer cream-plus-serif-plus-sage "tasteful default" that trading one default for another creates. Grounded in a 47-subreddit, 3.2M-post Reddit analysis of what people flag as AI slop. Use whenever building, styling, reviewing, refactoring, or auditing any website, landing page, web app UI, dashboard, or front-end component, especially when the user wants a site to look custom or human rather than AI-generated, or mentions AI slop, looks AI-made, generic, vibe-coded, Tailwind, or shadcn. Trigger even if they never say vibe-coded.

commands.name: skill:visualize
commands.description: Add a correct, minimal visual to a lesson — a diagram or geometric picture — that renders inline in the Obsidian log. Use when an idea is genuinely clearer as a picture: a dependency graph, system/flow, sequence, state machine, tree, comparison, or a spatial/geometric thing (coordinate geometry, number line, vectors, a plot, a physical layout). Outsources authoring+rendering to a maker subagent that verifies the image by looking at it, then you embed the returned file.
